title: Prod Launch Approval - Quickref RBAC2 & SIEM Export
content:
Purpose:
This quick reference is for release engineers, security owners, and product leads to validate RBAC v2 gating, capture automated evidence, and verify SIEM export mappings before a production go-live. It is intended as a compact checklist + runbook (not a replacement for the full release security playbook).

Scope:
- Applies to all production launches that modify serving topology, onboarding of new model variants, or deploy private/dedicated capacity that changes access controls or logging surface area.
- Covers RBAC v2 role bindings, audit log schema verification, automated evidence collection, and SIEM export sanity checks.

High-level owners (quick contact):
- Security owner: Sofia Patel (owner of this doc)
- Release lead: Andre Gomez
- SRE / Observability: Priya Raman
- Platform eng (RBAC runtime): Ethan Park
- Compliance reviewer: Maya Liu

Pre-launch checklist (must be completed before release window):
1) RBAC v2 gating
   - Confirm new roles/permissions are described in the ticket (JIRA-RINF-2142 or linked).
   - Verify least-privilege intent: every permission has a documented use-case.
   - Validate role bindings via dry-run: run `rbacctl validate --dry-run <manifest>` and confirm zero denies in the dry-run report.
   - Confirm separation-of-duty: deployer, approver, and auditor are distinct principals.
   - Ensure temporary-grants have TTL and documented justification.

2) Audit log schema and retention
   - Confirm schema version: audit_schema_version = v2.1 (fields below).
   - Check that the release adds no unlogged path (e.g., internal admin endpoints).
   - Verify retention policy for evidence bundle (default: 90 days unless higher compliance requires long-term storage).

3) Evidence automation run
   - Trigger evidence pipeline: `ci/evidence/run_release_evidence.sh --release <tag>` (CI job: release-evidence-collector).
   - Confirm collector produces an artifacts zip in GCS: gs://redwood-evidence/<release-tag>/evidence.zip.
   - Validate presence of required artifacts: role-manifests.yaml, policy-diff.txt, audit-sample.jsonl, siem-sample.json, signer-approvals.log.

4) SIEM export sanity check
   - Confirm SIEM connector staging run completed: job id `siem-export-<tag>-sanity-<ts>` in Observability.
   - Validate sample export landed in SIEM index (search query examples below).
   - Ensure mapping contains required fields and no PII in top-level event fields.

RBAC v2 gating checklist (detailed):
- Manifest names match service names (no wildcard role names in production).
- Policy diffs reviewed and signed off by platform eng (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/982).
- Delegated admin scopes limited to `team:platform-admin` for one-off tasks and logged with ticket id.
- Automated role reconciliation run (cron: rbac-reconcile-nightly) reported zero unexpected bindings.

Audit log schema (v2.1) - required fields and examples (single-line json example at end):
- event_id: uuid
- ts: iso8601 timestamp
- actor: {type, id} -> flattened field names used in SIEM: actor_type, actor_id
- action: string (e.g., role.assign, token.issue, model.deploy)
- target: {resource_type, resource_id} -> flattened: target_type, target_id
- decision: allow|deny|elevated
- reason: free text (optional but required for exception flows)
- request_id: correlation id across services
- request_metadata: flattened keys prefixed with meta_ (meta_ip, meta_user_agent)
- signature: base64 signature of event for non-repudiation (when available)

Example single-line event for SIEM ingest: 
{"event_id":"e3b0c4f2-...","ts":"2026-03-10T18:03:12Z","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"andre.gomez","action":"role.assign","target_type":"service-account","target_id":"svc-build-123","decision":"allow","reason":"approved-by-release-lead:JIRA-RINF-2142","request_id":"req-7f9c","meta_ip":"10.0.2.5","meta_user_agent":"rbacctl/1.2.0","signature":"MEUCIQ..."}

Evidence automation runbook (operational steps):
1) Kickoff: release lead creates ticket and triggers CI job `release-evidence-collector`. Include tag: release/<semver>.
2) Collector tasks:
   - Fetch all changed manifests from PR, run `policy-diff` against baseline (master).
   - Run `rbacctl simulate` across standard personas (deployer, support, auditor).
   - Pull last 48h of audit logs for the affected services using `audit-search --filter <resources> --since 48h` and write sample as jsonl.
   - Run SIEM connector in dry-run: map fields and push sample to SIEM test index.
3) Upload artifacts to evidence bucket and annotate the release ticket with the artifact location.
4) Automated validations that must pass (CI gates):
   - policy-diff contains no `*` wildcard grants.
   - all simulate runs return no unexpected deny for pre-approved flows and at least one deny for out-of-scope flows.
   - siem-sample.json passes schema validator (`tools/siem/validate_schema.py`).

Sign-off matrix (who signs and where):
- Security (S): must sign on ticket comment (Sofia Patel) with checklist completed and link to evidence zip.
- Release lead (R): confirm deployment window approved and sign on ticket (Andre Gomez).
- Observability (O): confirm SIEM export test success and index mapping (Priya Raman).
- Platform eng (P): confirm RBAC manifest merge and reconciliation results (Ethan Park).
- Compliance (C): final go/no-go for regulated customers when relevant (Maya Liu).

Exception approval flow (temporary roles / emergency exceptions):
- Exceptions must be requested in a ticket with tag `sec-exception` and include: justification, TTL (max 72 hours unless escalated), mitigation steps, and proposed audit capture.
- Triage: Security + Platform must review within 4 hours business SLA for critical exceptions.
- Approval: Security provides conditional approval only if automated evidence collection is enabled for the exception window and an auditor is assigned.
- Post-exception: evidence bundle must include role usage metrics and a replay of audit logs for the exception window.

Post-launch verification (first 72 hours):
- Nightly automated smoke: run `smoke-rbac-check --release <tag>` and post results to ticket.
- SIEM alerting: ensure key alert rules are firing (unauthorized role assignment, repeated denies, service-account elevation).
- One-week retrospective: security owner runs a short post-mortem if any anomalies.

Troubleshooting quick hits:
- If collector fails to find audit logs: verify service logging (env VAR AUDIT_COLLECTOR_ENABLED=true) and that the log forwarder is healthy.
- If siem-sample mapping fails: run `tools/siem/normalize.py` and re-run `validate_schema.py` to get actionable error lines.
- If RBAC reconcile reports drift: run `rbacctl diff --detailed` and attach output to ticket; platform eng to evaluate reconciliation policy.

Appendix - quick commands and locations:
- Run evidence collect: `./ci/evidence/run_release_evidence.sh --release release/1.4.0`
- Evidence bucket: gs://redwood-evidence/<release>/evidence.zip
- Audit search example: `audit-search --service serving-runtime --since 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z --query "action:role.assign"`
- SIEM validation script: tools/siem/validate_schema.py --input siem-sample.json
- RBAC dry-run: `rbacctl validate --manifest changed-roles.yaml`

Notes / open questions (working):
- Decide final default retention for evidence bundles for SOC2: 365 days vs. 90 days (compliance queue: JIRA-RINF-2301).
- Consider adding a short hash of evidence.zip to the ticket description for tamper-evident linkage.

This doc is intentionally compact; refer to Confluence page for RBAC v2 spec and full release-security playbook (linked above) for deep-dive procedures.

Last updated by: Sofia Patel on 2026-03-10
summary: Compact runbook and checklist to gate RBAC v2 changes, capture automated evidence, and verify SIEM export before production go-live. Draft for team review.
